requirement:
An outline input MUST be rewritten only if the mapped node exists and its
structural hash, computed under
{cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash` over the
{term}`requirements.refactor.mapped_back` text of the node, equals the recorded
hash.
rationale: The implementation in `src/refactor.rs#fn[rewrite_input]` (Outline arm, using `States::hash` and `OutlineCache::with_overrides(back)` built from `mappings.text_back`) meets both obligations. An absent mapped node gives an `Err` via `ParsedSource::resolve`, and no rewrite happens. The input is rewritten only when the mapped-back structural hash equals the recorded hash. Three tests cover the hash obligation: `a_moved_function_keeps_its_evidence_current` (match, rewritten), `a_function_edited_while_moving_leaves_its_records_stale` (mismatch, not rewritten) and `a_rename_rewrites_the_hash_of_a_node_whose_doc_comment_names_it` (mapped-back text decides the match). The gap is the failure case the text names, "the mapped node exists". No test with a {test} reference to this requirement runs `rewrite_input` with a mapped node that does not exist and checks that the input is not rewritten. The `fn[gone]` case in `invalid_mappings_fail_with_a_usage_error_and_change_nothing` is rejected earlier by mapping validation and is not referenced to this requirement. The `Err` branch for an unresolvable node is conditional code, so the missing-test exemption does not apply. No {fixme} acknowledges this gap.

text: :::{req} outline_inputs
An outline input MUST be rewritten only if the mapped node exists and its
structural hash, computed under
{cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash` over the
{term}`requirements.refactor.mapped_back` text of the node, equals the recorded
hash.
:::{req} structural_hash
A node's structural hash MUST be the SHA-256 digest of an unambiguous encoding of
its outline-relevant structure, including siblings its profile attaches to it:
the kinds of its named grammar nodes and, in source order, its text pieces. A
text piece MUST be the text of a leaf token, or text inside a node that no child
token covers. Each text piece MUST be hashed as its ordered list of words, where
words are separated by whitespace, the whitespace itself, including leading and
trailing whitespace, is never hashed, and each word is encoded separately, so
`ab cd` and `abcd` differ. The same rule MUST apply in every language. Comments
MUST be excluded, except comment kinds the profile includes; the Rust profile MUST include doc comments. For an included comment, only its text and its
profile's comment group MUST be hashed, not its delimiter tokens such as `//`,
`///`, `//!`, `/*`, `*/`, or a leading `*`; the Rust profile's groups are inner
and outer doc comments. The words of consecutive included comments of one group
MUST be hashed as one ordered list, so reflowing them across more or fewer lines
or comments does not change the hash, while moving text between groups does. A `line`
node's hash MUST be computed by the same word rule over the line's text. A node's
identity hash MUST be computed the same way but MUST also exclude its outline
descendants and their attached siblings, so editing a descendant does not change
its ancestors' selectors.
:::{definition} mapped_back
:phrase: mapped-back
The *mapped-back* form of current text or a current address is the text or
address with each new side of the mappings replaced by its old side.
